title: Connect a small browser page
summary: Run the optional Reading List page locally and call the C# API with fetch. Learn JSON, exact CORS origins and safe text rendering.
introduction: Our API can answer PowerShell. Now a small web page can use it too. The page has a title box, a read checkbox and a list. It sends HTTP requests to C#; it never needs the Oracle password.
learningObjectives: Serve the optional browser page on the allowed local origin
Send GET and POST requests with fetch
Keep passwords and untrusted HTML out of the browser

blocks.text: Allow the one local browser origin
Stop the API, open a terminal in ReadingListApi, and enable the optional development setting. Then restart using the same launch profile.

blocks.code:
dotnet user-secrets set "Development:CorsEnabled" "true"
dotnet run --launch-profile ReadingListApi
blocks.title: Enable the local browser demo

blocks.text: The API allows http://localhost:5500 only in Development. An **origin** is the scheme, host and port together. localhost and 127.0.0.1 are different origins, and port 5501 is different from 5500. Match the address exactly.

Use a static file server for the browser-client folder on port 5500. If Python 3 is installed, run this in another terminal from the extracted sample root. A code editor's local web server can also serve that folder at the same address.

Open http://localhost:5500 in your browser. Do not double-click index.html: a file:// page has a different origin. The page can list and add books; the API's update and delete actions can still be tested with PowerShell.

blocks.title: The GET idea
blocks.caption: Run this inside an async function, as in browser-client/app.js. This excerpt is not a standalone script.

blocks.text: fetch sends the request. Check response.ok because a reply such as HTTP 500 is still a reply. response.json reads the JSON body. The complete app.js handles errors and lets the learner try Refresh list again.

blocks.title: The POST idea
blocks.caption: This belongs inside an async function. The downloaded app.js checks the reply before showing success.

blocks.title: Display one title safely
blocks.caption: Here book is one API result and list is the page's list element.

blocks.text: textContent shows the title as text. Do not put a book title into innerHTML, because a title is not trusted page markup. If someone types Book, those characters should appear as the title rather than becoming a bold HTML element.

blocks.title: CORS is not a password
blocks.text: CORS is a browser rule about which origins may read a reply. It does not stop PowerShell or other clients from calling an API. This local sample has no sign-in and must not be treated as a protected public service.
Add a book in the local page, then request /api/books from PowerShell. Both should show the same Oracle data. Stop the API and use Refresh list to see the page's useful error message.
